Impacted Systems: PyTorch-nightly users who installed the package between December 25th and December 30th, 2022
Attack Vector: The malicious 'torchtriton' package was being installed instead of the version from PyTorch's official repository due to PyPI index taking precedence
Indicators of Compromise: The malicious 'torchtriton' dependency had exceeded 2,300 downloads in the past week
The malicious 'triton' binary contained within the counterfeit 'torchtriton' is only executed when the user imports 'triton' package in their build

The malicious binary collects system information and reads several files including /etc/hosts, /etc/passwd, the first 1,000 files in $HOME/*, $HOME/.gitconfig, $HOME/.ssh/* and uploads all of this data to the h4ck.cfd domain via encrypted DNS queries using the wheezy.io DNS server
The SHA256 hash of the 'triton' ELF binary is: 2385b29489cd9e35f92c072780f903ae2e517ed422eae67246ae50a5cc738a0e
